speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, if I may begin in Mandarin.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, last year, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) and SMRT built a new overhead bridge at the Clementi Town Centre.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This overhead bridge enables residents to walk from Block 326 to Clementi Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station, crossing Commonwealth Avenue West conveniently and safely.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: With the new overhead bridge, the old pedestrian crossing at the ground level and the traffic lights were removed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: On the surface, this new facility seems to be perfect.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Pedestrians do not have to wait for the traffic lights to turn green; they can simply use the overhead bridge to cross the road.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: There are even lifts at the overhead bridge so that our elderly residents can enjoy barrier-free access.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: However, what was meant to be a perfect facility has, in fact, some shortcomings.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The overhead bridge, therefore, has inadvertently become a new barrier.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some Clementi residents are wondering why this is so.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have appealed to LTA on behalf of the residents but six months have passed and the problem is still not solved.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In response to my query, LTA replied that since there is only one SMRT staff at the MRT station in the middle of the night, should there be a lift breakdown, that one staff would not be able to provide emergency assistance.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This answer sounds plausible but does not make sense.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Lifts in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates operate round-the-clock.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Anytime when there is a lift breakdown, we can call the 24-hour Emergency Maintenance Services Unit (EMSU) service for emergency repairs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Is there such a big difference between the lifts in HDB estates and those at overhead bridges?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: How come HDB estate lifts can operate 24 hours, yet lifts at overhead bridges cannot?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some people might say: "This is such a small matter pertaining to Clementi, why do you have to raise this issue in Parliament?" Deputy Speaker, Sir, I think this matter actually reflects the style of some Government agencies in terms of policy design and implementation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I am more concerned that this could well be just the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Hence, I sincerely hope that LTA can resolve this problem as soon as possible to make this nice, albeit slightly flawed, overhead bridge into one that is perfect and can provide 24-hour barrier-free access.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, whether in the public or private sectors, policy and implementation are about the big and the small.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Sometimes, you can see a universe in a raindrop, or, sometimes, you see a world in a grain of sand.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But it is in the little details that we see deep lessons about the broader firmament.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, if I may beg the indulgence of Deputy Speaker, I will mention a few local examples to highlight issues of national policy and implementation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In 2015, the LTA and SMRT opened a new sheltered overhead link bridge along Commonwealth Avenue West.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It connects Clementi Block 326 to the MRT station.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The old pedestrian crossing at ground-level was removed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My Clementi residents with mobility needs now have to find a different place to cross the road when they venture out at night.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I am sure LTA and SMRT had the best of intentions, but the devil is in the details.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Whenever a ground-level signal crossing is replaced, surely the new facility should be as good, or even better, in providing access to Singaporeans with mobility needs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: When we add new innovations, we must be mindful not to subtract from it what came before, especially when it affects the vulnerable and disadvantaged among us.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have appealed to LTA which has consulted with SMRT.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was told that, after revenue hours, there is only one station staff member preparing for the next morning's operation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, the agencies are worried about what might happen if there is a lift breakdown with a trapped pedestrian.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But, Deputy Speaker, I draw a comparison with our HDB estates where the lifts do not shut down overnight.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: If a HDB lift breaks down, emergency assistance is despatched through EMSU 24 hours a day.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Surely, SMRT and LTA could find a similar arrangement to cater for residents with mobility needs, especially after the pedestrian crossing at ground level was removed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I understand that resources may be limited and, if this is a concern, perhaps SMRT could partner with the existing EMSU framework to achieve economies of scale.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: There are many possible back-end solutions to look after our residents at the frontline.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, I am sure a solution can be found and that measures can be taken to prevent similar situations from arising.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I know SMRT and LTA are working very hard on this.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My residents tell me a solution cannot arrive too soon and we must make sure other HDB town centres do not face the same problem.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to speak as well on another area where we could have better pedestrian access.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some of our HDB town centres have a lot of pedestrian and vehicular traffic.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It makes sense to create a network of overhead pedestrian bridges, helping pedestrians cross from HDB blocks to shopping malls, away from vehicular traffic.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This improves accessibility for the elderly as well as young families with prams.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It also helps drivers when pedestrians and traffic are separated from each other.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, commercial developers benefit when a new building is located in an HDB town centre, especially in a mature estate with a critical mass of residents and customers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The central location and population density bring business opportunities for any landlord.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But if developer and landlord are benefiting from the HDB town centre location, surely there is a responsibility to contribute back to the community?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We should not have a situation where the benefits and profits are privatised with hardly any socialisation of the gains.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Indeed, the Building Code helps prevent market failure which occurs when developers prioritise profit and rents over the broader public good.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: This is why in 1990, the first Building Code on Barrier-Free Accessibility was introduced.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Since then, barrier-free access has improved significantly in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to elaborate on another issue which my colleague in Parliament Mr Ang Wei Neng had raised as a Parliamentary Question: how our MRT stations connect to public hospitals.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Visiting a sick relative in hospital can be a stressful time for the family.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The least we can do is to make the journey smoother, less exposed to weather and less open to the elements.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some of our public hospitals already have such sheltered barrier-free access from the nearest MRT station.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Tan Tock Seng Hospital connects with Novena MRT Station.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The National University Hospital's new medical centre links with Kent Ridge MRT Station.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Ng Teng Fong General Hospital has overhead walkways in Jurong to avoid the traffic at ground level.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Singapore General Hospital is connected to Outram Park MRT Station, but the main challenge is that the hospital is still some distance away, although the SGH Campus Masterplan – I understand – will address this in years to come.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But KK Women's and Children's Hospital is not quite there yet, nor is Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Here, there is, again, a role for enhancing covered barrier-free access so that patients and their relatives can have one less thing to worry about when visiting their sick relatives in our public hospitals.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, these stories are a link and a bridge to a broader issue and a bigger picture.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Our public servants and agencies work very hard.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They mean well, but governance has gotten more complicated.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Many areas of specialisation, much more happening at the same time, issues needing coordination and many policy issues straddle the public and private sectors as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In dealing with this complexity, design is crucial.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: We can draw lessons from other sectors, for example, portable digital devices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Thoughtful people-centric design is what differentiated the Apple iPhone and iPod from the rest of the industry, from their competitors.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Attention to the whole user experience making sure individual elements add up to more than the sum of individual parts, first-mile and last-mile, not just for the journey as a whole, but also where each component connects to each other.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Imagine if we had a "design language" that guides how we help pedestrians navigate new towns and redevelop mature town centres.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In this design language, each agency and each component is like one letter of the alphabet, one word in the dictionary.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And when we put it all together, we must be able to make beautiful poetry, not just turgid technical prose.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Deputy Speaker, even as we build deep expertise in specialist areas, even as we add new technology and new construction, we must never lose sight that the people are at the heart of all we do.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So long as we continue seeing through the eyes of the people, we will continue being able to build better homes and a better Singapore.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think Minister Wong would want to reply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I fully agree with him that we must adopt a people-centric approach when designing and planning our city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, our city planners are fully aware that the work they do is not just a technical exercise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because we know that even as we build and shape our infrastructure, it is our infrastructure that shapes us.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It influences our actions, our behaviours and our mindsets.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A well-designed city can inspire us, it can lift our spirits.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Conversely, in a poorly-designed city, life can be brutish and miserable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the approach that the Government has taken from our early years of nation-building has always been to put people at the centre of urban planning.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can see this from the very First Concept Plan which was formulated in 1971.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have looked at the concept plan then.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The centre of our island was preserved as a natural reserve and water catchment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We pushed out the heavy industrial areas from residential areas so that pollution will be kept away from the people and then we had lighter industry and commercial areas planned adjacent to new towns so that people do not have to travel far to get to the Central Business District (CBD) to work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These were some of the features in our First Concept Plan more than 40 years ago.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But these essential features are still very much recognisable in the structure of Singapore today.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just about the big picture of a concept plan but also focusing on details, as Dr Tan Wu Meng has mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A good example of that is having a clean and green environment for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is something that we put a lot of attention to, it was not just slogan or window-dressing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was a strategic imperative and one which we set about doing deliberately year after year, and putting a lot of attention to details.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Lee Kuan Yew had always emphasised, having public access to greenery is nothing less than a matter of a social equity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about creating a sense of social equalness in society so that everyone, regardless of where you stay, be it a flat, a condominium or a landed property, everyone in Singapore can have equal access to greenery and public spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the point I wanted to highlight, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, is that we have always put people first in our planning considerations and this will continue to be our approach as we think about planning our city going forward.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to continue with our long-term plans to make good use of spaces, we will have to continue with our greening initiatives and, indeed, as we look forward to the next phase of urban planning, we want to make significant enhancements to pedestrian connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, one key priority for us is to improve our pedestrian connectivity, to improve first-mile, last-mile connections and to ensure that our environment is highly walkable in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a long-term effort which will require many stakeholders and involve many implementation details.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But let me just share some broad areas of emphasis and also, in doing so, respond to some of the suggestions that the Member has highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can already see some of these taking shape, say, in a town like Jurong.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you come out from the Jurong East MRT, you will see elevated walkways which allow commuters direct access to the nearby malls like JEM and Westgate and, potentially, to other key developments that are coming up in the future Jurong Lake district.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, that is the first point – that we are going to have more pedestrian connections.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we are going to improve the walking experience.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So it is not just about having more connections but, as Dr Tan Wu Meng has highlighted, about having better-designed walkways so that we can create a more comfortable and a more user-friendly walking environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One important priority is to enhance the linkages to MRT stations and bus interchanges with better covered walkways.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, there will be an expansion and there will be more covered walkways linking to MRT stations to enhance the walking experience and the last-mile, first-mile connections.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng mentioned that there are covered walkways from MRT Stations to most public hospitals but he highlighted two in particular, that are not directly connected – the KK Women's and Children's Hospital and the Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, it is slightly further away from the MRT station because the hospital was built in a mature estate where there was not an available site near to the MRT.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the hospital is now about 700 metres away from the MRT station, about a 15-minute walk.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within our housing estates, HDB is also working on a more integrated network of pedestrian connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, this will be done for all new estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The walkability features will be incorporated into the design of all new estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For existing estates, the improvements can be done as part of our upgrading programmes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) which estates can make use of to enhance pedestrian connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as all Members in this House are involved in the NRP implementation process through the Town Councils, I would encourage everyone to think about how you can prioritise the use of your NRP funds towards enhancing pedestrian connectivity within your estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, all Members in this House have the responsibility and also the ability, through the NRP funding, to enhance pedestrian connectivity within your own towns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another way of enhancing pedestrian experience is to better meet the needs of the elderly and the vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: LTA is continuing with efforts to install lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges to improve barrier-free access to public transport nodes and popular destinations.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the issue of lifts, Dr Tan Wu Meng highlighted the case at Clementi MRT where LTA provided the lift and then the lift only works during MRT operating hours.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I checked with LTA and I think they have also done their checks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, he can convey the good news to his residents in both English and Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just in Clementi, because LTA will be learning from this example and experience to make sure that solutions are available not just in Clementi but in other towns as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, that is the second point about enhancing the pedestrian experience.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Thirdly, as highlighted by Dr Tan Wu Meng, the private sector also plays an important role in realising our people-centric vision of pedestrian connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is already done today – Government agencies work with developers to safeguard pedestrian access through private developments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is possible for new developments; it is harder and more complex to do so for existing ones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a complex issue and we are studying this very carefully.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It may or may not be legislation of powers needed in the Building Code.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There could be other forms of legislative levers that we can apply and, so, that is a matter being studied and the details will be announced in due course.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of this is work-in-progress and it is a long-term effort.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires support and understanding from all stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng spoke about having a "design language" in which we can think about designing our streets better for pedestrian connectivity and I fully agree with him.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Having such a design language, in fact, requires us to think about taking some hard decisions because designing a city for people and for walkability potentially means reducing car parking norms; it means, shrinking road sizes; it means pedestrianising more roads.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those are the hard decisions that we may have to make.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other road users would have to make adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I note that we have received – both the Ministry of National Development (MND) and Ministry of Transport (MOT) – many requests from the public, including from Members of this House, from time to time to have more car parks, not just more car parks but more free car parks, which will just add to road users but for cars, not for pedestrians and sometimes to expand the roads for cars.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are issues that we have to balance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we truly want to embrace a more pedestrian-friendly culture, it is really about adopting a more car-lite culture in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You can come to the civic district, the roads are closed, you can walk, you can cycle, you can jog, you can enjoy the streets, for people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I would welcome Members to participate and join us on the last Sunday of the month to experience what car-free Sunday is about.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why, despite our constraints, we have today a city in a garden and we have people from all over the world coming to MND, URA and MOT to learn about our experience.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The nature of urban planning is such that it is really long-term work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It takes good planning; it takes systematic implementation over many years and even decades.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, you cannot look at urban planning over just one or even two electoral cycles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: You have to think and plan long-term and then implement and deliver the results systematically and progressively.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is what we have done in Singapore and that is what we will continue to do.
